instruction: nx.edge_betweenness_centrality(G, k=...) ignores k when it rescales. With k sampled source nodes, only k of the n sources contribute, so: unnormalized values must be scaled by n/k (and, as now, halved for undirected graphs) to estimate the values over all sources, and normalized values must be divided by the number of (source, target) pairs actually considered, k * (n - 1), instead of n * (n - 1). For example nx.path_graph(3) with k=2 and seed=42 samples the sources 0 and 2; each edge then lies on three of their shortest paths, so normalized=False gives {(0, 1): 9/4, (1, 2): 9/4} and normalized=True gives {(0, 1): 3/4, (1, 2): 3/4}. Results without k don't change, and node betweenness_centrality with k must keep its current results. Also, with sources and targets both all nodes and normalized=True, betweenness_centrality_subset and edge_betweenness_centrality_subset must give the same values as betweenness_centrality(G) and edge_betweenness_centrality(G). Add tests.
